text:
mina: FYI customers keep tripping over import style in our JS SDK. They post snippets like `const SDK = require('@redwood/inference')` then `SDK.createClient` is undefined.

rob: That's an interop mismatch. If we publish ESM with a default export, `require()` returns an object where the default is on `.default`. So `require(...).default.createClient` might work, but it's messy.

casey: Docs idea: three clear examples only - Node CJS, Node ESM, Edge ESM - plus a tiny TS note. Keep it short.

mina: Examples we should show: 
1) Node CJS (no "type":"module")
`const { createClient } = require('@redwood/inference')`
2) Node ESM (`"type":"module"`)
`import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'`
3) Edge (Cloudflare/Vercel/Bun/Deno)
`import createClient from '@redwood/inference'` or named import depending on export.

rob: Also add a one-line runtime normalizer snippet for lib authors: `const _all = await import('@redwood/inference'); const R = _all.default || _all;` then use `R.createClient`. That handles most cases.

casey: TS note: `esModuleInterop: true` makes `import Redwood from '...'` compile, but it can hide ESM-only runtime failures. Call that out.

mina: Small package.json `exports` example to include in docs so resolution is deterministic: "exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs" } }.

docs-bot: Opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/470 - added examples + troubleshooting checklist.

mina: Great. Add a troubleshooting checklist: check runtime (edge vs node), check tsconfig flags, try `import * as` fallback, try `require(...).default` to diagnose.

casey: Also recommend named exports as preferred stable API surface.

rob: I'll review the PR and add a tiny compatibility table for major runtimes.

mina: Thanks team :)
